content:
The image shows a sugarcane leaf laid flat, displaying a distinctive bicolor striping pattern:
- A green band running along the midrib/upper surface
- A pale yellow-cream/white band on the lower surface
- Tan/yellow-orange coloration along the margins

**Analysis against each class:**

- **Brown_Spot**: No brown lesions or spots are visible — ruled out.
- **Grassy_Shoot**: This condition shows excessive thin shoot proliferation, not leaf discoloration patterns — ruled out.
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Typically shows chlorotic wedge-shaped distortion or twisting of young leaves at the shoot — not consistent with this flat, stripe-patterned leaf.
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Classic symptom is yellowing of the midrib on the abaxial (lower/underside) surface of sugarcane leaves, while the adaxial (upper) surface retains green coloration. This image clearly shows exactly that — green upper surface with a bright yellow-cream lower surface/midrib stripe. This is the hallmark of Sugarcane Yellow Leaf Virus (SCYLV).

The stripe pattern (green top, yellow-cream underside) is a textbook presentation of Yellow Leaf disease in sugarcane.
